responsibility: This file is the main top-level driver for LTO execution modes inside lto1. Its lto_main orchestrates the three personalities described by the module—full LTO, WPA, and LTRANS—by initializing the shared LTO front end, reading merged symbols/callgraph state, materializing function bodies when needed, invoking whole-program analysis versus direct compilation, handling OpenMP/offload link-variable setup, driving partition streaming for WPA output files, and emitting final LTO reports. It is therefore the control-flow coordinator for optimization and partition write-out, unlike lto-common.c which provides the shared stream-in/runtime services beneath it.
same_name_distinction: This is the executable driver side of the lto pair: it implements lto_main and orchestrates LTO/WPA/LTRANS control flow, body materialization, partition write-out, and reporting, whereas gcc/lto/lto.h is the module interface header that defines shared LTO types and declares module-wide APIs.
